Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

eventclock 0.6.0

Ordinary-risk benchmark from quiet-clock surfaces

  • ec_quiet_library() builds the library of earlier option surfaces: at-the-money volatility, smile shape relative to at-the-money (difference or ratio), calendar days to expiry, and the Event Clock realized over each surface’s own remaining life (from event prices, optionally on staggered intraday grids, or supplied).
  • ec_quiet_rules() fixes the template-rule grid in advance: quietness threshold (quantile of the available clocks or absolute) × days-to-expiry band × aggregation (all, most recent n, n nearest by at-the-money volatility). The defaults are the 15-rule grid; the 30-rule variant is one call.
  • ec_quiet_shape() predicts a target’s smile shape under each rule from templates that expired at or before the target date; the target contributes only its date, expiry, and at-the-money level.
  • ec_quiet_select() chooses the rule by cross-validation on earlier pseudo-targets (maturity block left out; optionally only templates available at each pseudo-target date; optionally only pseudo-targets with a minimum days to expiry, pseudo_min_dte), with wing-shape RMSE over 0.04 <= |k| <= 0.30 (or 0.5 <= |z| <= 3 in standardized moneyness, k / (ATM volatility × sqrt(tau))), a common node set across rules, and the target’s predicted shape under every rule.

Exchange option data

  • cme_definitions(), cme_statistics(), cme_option_surfaces() turn CME Globex instrument definitions and daily statistics (Databento’s GLBX.MDP3 schemas, as Parquet or CSV files or data frames) into option surfaces: last final settlement per trading date, futures settlement as forward, time to the published expiration, Black (1976) implied volatilities (both sides and out-of-the-money), vega, open interest, a put-call parity diagnostic, exercise style from the CFI code, inverted quotes (invert = TRUE), and the event probability at the valuation time. Files whose columns all arrived as text read the same as typed files. The output feeds ec_theta_fit() and ec_quiet_library() directly. No exchange data ships with the package.
  • The exchange reuses instrument identifiers after a contract expires or is deleted (a call can become a put, a spread an option). cme_definitions() therefore returns one row per identifier phase (valid_from, valid_to, deleted), and cme_option_surfaces() attributes each daily statistic to the phase in force on its trading date; the output names the contracts used (call_symbol, put_symbol).

eventclock 0.5.0

Bug fix

  • event_beta() now takes the probability level at each asset date (the last observation on or before it) and differences it between consecutive asset dates. Previously probability changes were computed on the calendar-daily series before matching, so moves over weekends and holidays were lost: a Monday return was paired with the Sunday-to-Monday change only. On the shipped DJT/Polymarket example the exposure estimate rises from 1.28 (t = 2.6) to 1.47 (t = 3.9).

Synchronization with the current working paper

  • ec_recovery_set() now uses the paper’s notation: the partial-recovery bound is delta (the old argument eps still works with a deprecation warning; the output column is now delta). The documentation states the bound exactly as in the paper — valuation variation at most delta^2 times the measured log-odds variation — and explains the low-clock endpoint (1 - delta)^2.
  • The companion working paper The Event Clock: What State Prices Identify About Physical Information (SSRN 7420838) is now cited in citation("eventclock"), the README, and the vignettes; the package version in the citation is read from DESCRIPTION.
  • “Event Clock” is capitalized throughout, as in the papers (“event-clock time” stays lower case).
  • ec_iv_rule() is documented as the first-order screening formula; the exact pre-resolution value is ec_mix_iv_pre(), which reproduces the paper’s Brexit two-week learning contribution (0.0083 IV points).
  • Golden tests relabeled: Brexit 1W/2W/1M clocks are the paper’s main-text numbers; robustness variants are pinned against earlier versions’ reference values; the trailing-60 real-time forecast reproduces the paper’s 2016 values (0.0476 / 0.0951) to within 1%.

Measuring the clock in practice

  • event_clock_forecast() is rebuilt around the paper’s no-look-ahead forecast: estimation windows in trailing observations (default, unchanged results), trailing calendar days (days = 3 with hourly data), or the whole history (expanding = TRUE); any estimator (method); optional staggered sampling (interval). New output columns rule and rate_per_day.
  • ec_forecast_rules() and ec_forecast_select() choose the forecasting rule by out-of-sample RMSE on earlier option lives only. On the shipped data they reproduce the working paper’s choices: trailing-60 realized variation for the 2016 daily series, and a trailing three-day window for hourly Polymarket prices with weekly option lives in 2024.
  • event_clock_staggered() — clocks on staggered time grids (e.g. 30-, 60-, 120-minute sampling averaged over all grid offsets), with the estimator applied within each grid.
  • event_clock_venues() / event_clock_venues_path() — clocks from two venues: each venue’s own clock, the equal-weight composite, and the cross-venue clock that filters venue-specific noise; reports increment correlation and each venue’s noise share.

Option-implied exposure and a second venue

  • ec_theta_fit() gains a date-block (moving-block) bootstrap for the common exposure (boot_reps, block, block_length, conf), the working paper’s inference for the conditional-mean ratio; per-node fitted values and residuals ($nodes); and, when bid and ask implied volatilities are supplied, the share of fitted values inside the quotes ($inside_share).
  • Kalshi connector: ks_events(), ks_markets(), ks_prices() on the public, keyless trade API (live and settled markets, chunked candlesticks, last-trade or mid prices), returning event_prices objects.
  • New dataset kalshi2024: daily 15:45 New York snapshot of the Kalshi Trump-win contract, October 4 to November 5, 2024 — the second venue for event_clock_venues().

Pricing, data, and documentation

  • ec_mix_price_pre() / ec_mix_iv_pre() — exact pre-resolution option prices under event learning: the future event probability follows the maintained two-component logistic-normal transition, ordinary risk is an independent lognormal, and A = 0 collapses to the fixed-probability (no-learning) Black benchmark. Completes the pricing side of the framework; the first-order formula-book versions (ec_sigma_eff(), ec_iv_rule()) remain as back-of-the-envelope checks.
  • The event-spanning vignette was rewritten for general readers: motivation without paper context, an explicit “what you need” section, and a new pre-resolution pricing section.
  • README gains a workflow section mapping the paper’s sequential architecture (probability -> clock -> validation -> returns-based exposure -> option-implied exposure -> learning test) to functions and vignettes.
  • pkgdown now renders help-page math via MathJax (previously raw LaTeX appeared on reference pages).
  • New dataset us2016_surfaces_sim: simulated event-spanning delta-grid surfaces matching the S&P 500 profile over the last four weeks before the 2016 U.S. election (47 surfaces, common exposure theta = -0.077). Fully synthetic — generated from the event mixture with fitted parameters as calibration targets — and the worked real-scale example of the event-spanning vignette.

eventclock 0.4.0

Event-spanning options

  • ec_mix_price() / ec_mix_iv() — forward-normalized option prices and Black implied dispersions under the two-component lognormal event mixture (outcome-conditional means parametrized by the event exposure theta = log(m1/m2) under the pricing-measure adding-up normalization).
  • ec_theta_fit() — the common conditional-mean-ratio design: per-surface outcome-conditional dispersions, one event exposure theta across all event-spanning surfaces (surface-balanced IV objective); common = FALSE gives the free-ratio diagnostic.
  • ec_theta_hump() — first-order |theta| from the spanning total-variance hump, sqrt(dvar / (q (1 - q))); the quick estimator on top of an existing maturity-hump pipeline.
  • ec_delta_to_k() — call-equivalent delta grid to log-forward moneyness.

Event clock

  • ec_recovery_set() — the sharp partial-recovery interval [(1 - eps)_+^2 A, (1 + eps)^2 A] for the physical event clock, the working paper’s sensitivity grid around exact recovery.

eventclock 0.3.0

Assets & finance

  • event_beta() — realized-loading regression of asset returns on event-probability news, with a base-R Newey-West (Bartlett/HAC) covariance, model-implied outcome levels under the risk-neutral adding-up constraint, and — given an externally measured exposure via deta — the loading test of beta = 1.
  • ec_relevance() — the sufficient statistic for whether event learning is first-order for an asset’s option prices; ties out exactly with ec_variance_share() and ec_iv_rule().
  • q_from_ffutures() — meeting-implied probabilities from 30-day fed funds futures on the standard month-average extraction, with the new fomc_meetings calendar dataset (2021-2027).
  • q_from_deal_spread() — completion probabilities from merger-arb spreads: deal clocks feed the same q -> logit -> A pipeline.
  • New dataset djt2024 (daily DJT prices, June-November 2024) powering the event-beta example against polymarket2024.

eventclock 0.2.0

Inference & validation

  • event_clock(se = TRUE) — standard errors and confidence intervals for the realized-variation estimate, via the quarticity analogue (log-based intervals) or a moment-matched wild bootstrap (se_method = "bootstrap").
  • ec_signature() and plot_signature() — the sampling-frequency signature plot of the clock (subsample-averaged), the standard microstructure-noise diagnostic.
  • ec_validate() — data-quality report for event-probability series: coverage, staleness, tick size, gaps, and outliers, in the flag-don’t-drop spirit.
  • ec_simulate_path() gains jump_share/n_jumps for lumpy information arrival (Bayes-consistent per step), the testbed for the jump-robust estimator variants.
  • New vignette “Validating the event-clock estimator” (Monte Carlo: consistency, CI coverage, outcome-independence/measure robustness, bipower under jumps, microstructure and the snapshot rule).
  • CI now runs the full R CMD check including vignettes on a three-OS matrix in a non-UTC timezone, plus a coverage job.

eventclock 0.1.0 (initial version)

New features

  • Initial version of the package.
  • as_event_prices() turns any data.frame/tibble of traded event probabilities into a standardized event_prices object with flag-don’t-drop cleaning (q_from_price() handles discount and overround normalization).
  • event_clock() estimates event-clock (information) time A as the realized variation of log-odds, with truncation, bipower, and largest-move robustness variants; event_clock_path() returns the cumulative clock; event_clock_forecast() implements the trailing-window real-time benchmark.
  • Formula-book calculators ec_moments(), ec_exceedance(), ec_revision(), ec_atm_event_call(), ec_sigma_eff(), ec_variance_share(), ec_iv_rule(), and ec_target_clock().
  • Exact logistic-normal transition tools ec_transition_density(), ec_simulate(), and ec_simulate_path().
  • Polymarket connector pm_search(), pm_markets(), pm_prices(), and pm_daily() built on the public Gamma and CLOB APIs.
  • Plotting helpers plot_q(), plot_clock(), and plot_clock_vs_calendar().
  • Datasets brexit2016 and us2016 reproducing the headline event-clock estimates of the accompanying working paper.
